gaps.sentence: I only need ___ few more minutes to finish.
gaps.explanation: 'A few minutes' = some minutes; 'few' alone would mean almost none.

gaps.sentence: The tour included ___ visit to the British Museum.
gaps.explanation: 'A visit' (one of many possible) and 'the British Museum' (museums take 'the').

gaps.sentence: We had ___ wonderful time in Prague.
gaps.explanation: 'Have a wonderful/great/good time' — 'time' here is countable and takes 'a'.

gaps.sentence: He was sent to ___ prison for armed robbery.
gaps.explanation: 'Be sent to prison' (as a prisoner) takes no article; visiting the building is 'go to the prison'.

gaps.sentence: He joined ___ army when he was eighteen.
gaps.explanation: Institutions take 'the': the army, the police, the church.

gaps.sentence: ___ water in this bottle tastes strange.
gaps.explanation: The of/in-phrase makes the noun definite: the water in this bottle.

gaps.sentence: His wife goes to ___ prison every Sunday to visit him.
gaps.explanation: Here 'the prison' is the building she visits, not the institution of imprisonment.

gaps.sentence: She gets up at six and watches ___ morning news.
gaps.explanation: 'The morning news' — a specific known broadcast, so 'the'.
